unit_label: Module C unit 8 (courseware unit 24), part 1: stressed assets, wilful defaulters, options for stressed assets, recovery forums, compromise settlements and technical write-offs

facts.statement: Credit default means the inability or unwillingness of a customer or counterparty to meet commitments in relation to lending, trading or any other financial transactions. It may take these forms: in direct lending, principal or interest not repaid as per the terms; in guarantees or letters of credit, funds not forthcoming from the constituents upon crystallisation of the liability; in treasury operations, the payment or series of payments due from counterparties under the contracts not forthcoming or ceasing; in securities trading businesses, funds or securities settlement not effected; and in cross-border exposure, the availability and free transfer of foreign currency funds ceasing or restrictions being imposed by the sovereign. Stressed assets are those in which the default has already occurred or which face a reasonably certain prospect of default; for example, a term loan for an industrial project whose implementation has been abandoned is a stressed asset even though the repayment has not yet fallen due. The Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) is the ratio of provisioning to gross non-performing assets and indicates the extent of funds a bank has kept aside to cover loan losses.

Under the 2025 Directions a wilful default by a borrower is deemed to have occurred when the borrower defaults in meeting payment or repayment obligations to the lender and any one or more of these features is noticed: the borrower has the capacity to honour the obligations; has diverted the funds availed under the credit facility; has siphoned off the funds; has disposed of immovable or movable assets provided for securing the credit facility without the lender's approval; or the borrower or promoter has failed in its commitment to infuse equity despite having the ability, although the lender provided loans or concessions based on this commitment. For a guarantor, wilful default occurs if the guarantor does not honour the guarantee when invoked despite having sufficient means, or disposes of assets provided for securing the facility without approval, or fails in a commitment to infuse equity. A wilful defaulter is a borrower or guarantor who has committed wilful default with an outstanding amount of Rs 25 lakh and above (or as notified by RBI), and, where the borrower is a company, its promoters and directors (subject to paragraph 5(14)), or, for an entity other than a company, the persons in charge and responsible for its management. A large defaulter is one with an outstanding amount of Rs 1 crore and above and where a suit has been filed or whose account is classified as doubtful or loss.
facts.locator: RBI_WD_2025 paragraph 3(1)(xi), (xviii) and (xix); S01 printed p. 513

facts.statement: Diversion of funds includes: utilisation of short-term working capital funds for long-term purposes not in conformity with the terms of sanction; deploying borrowed funds for activities or creation of assets other than those for which the credit was sanctioned; transferring borrowed funds to subsidiaries, group companies or other entities by whatever modality without the approval of the bank or all lenders in a consortium; routing funds through any lender other than the bank or consortium members without prior written permission; investing borrowed funds in other companies by acquiring equities or debt instruments without lender approval; and a shortfall in deployment of funds against the amounts disbursed or drawn with the difference not accounted for. Siphoning of funds occurs if any funds availed from the bank are utilised for purposes unrelated to the operations of the borrower; whether a case amounts to siphoning is a judgement of the lenders based on objective facts and circumstances.
facts.locator: RBI_WD_2025 paragraph 3(1)(vii) and (xvi); S01 printed p. 513

facts.statement: A bank identifies a wilful defaulter by a procedure that looks at the track record of the borrower and not isolated transactions, and the default must be intentional, deliberate and calculated. An Identification Committee examines the evidence; if satisfied it issues a show-cause notice (borrower, guarantor, promoter, directors or persons in charge) with all material relied on and calls for submissions within 21 days; it then proposes classification to a Review Committee with written reasons; the person has 15 days to make a written representation to the Review Committee, which also gives an opportunity for a personal hearing; the process is in-house, so there is no right to be represented by a lawyer; the Review Committee passes a reasoned order that is communicated. The Identification Committee is chaired by a whole-time director other than the MD and CEO with two senior officials; the Review Committee by the MD and CEO with two independent or non-executive directors, and its members are not part of the Identification Committee. A non-whole-time, independent or nominee director is not treated as a wilful defaulter unless it is conclusively established that the default took place with their consent or connivance or that they knew of it from board minutes and did not record an objection. A bank examines wilful default in all NPA accounts with outstanding of Rs 25 lakh and above, and where it is observed completes the classification within six months of the account being classified as NPA.

Penal measures against any person or entity classified as a wilful defaulter by any lender: no additional credit facility to the wilful defaulter or any entity with which it is associated, a bar that continues for one year after the name is removed from the List of Wilful Defaulters; no credit facility for floating new ventures for five years after removal; and restructuring only as the Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions permit. A company is associated with a wilful defaulter company if it is a subsidiary, joint venture or associate company; for a natural person, entities in which he is a promoter, director or in charge of management are associated. A bank includes a covenant that the borrower will not induct a person whose name is in the list on its board or management, and under no circumstances renews, enhances, gives fresh credit or restructures facilities for such a borrower while a promoter, director or person in charge remains in the list. A bank initiates legal action where warranted. The Board policy sets non-discriminatory criteria for publishing photographs of wilful defaulters. A guarantor who refuses to honour a demand may itself be classified as a wilful defaulter, and a group company whose guarantee for a wilfully defaulting unit is not honoured when invoked is also considered.

A bank reports to all credit information companies at monthly intervals the list of large defaulters (suit-filed accounts, and non-suit-filed accounts classified doubtful or loss) and the list of wilful defaulters (suit-filed and non-suit-filed). The threshold for large defaulters includes unapplied interest. The name of a wilful defaulter is removed within thirty days after the outstanding falls below Rs 25 lakh, but in a compromise settlement the name stays until the borrower has fully paid the compromise amount. Before transferring a defaulted loan of Rs 25 lakh and above, the bank examines it from a wilful default perspective and, if wilful default is observed, completes classification and reports before the transfer. The bank includes the Director Identification Number (DIN) among the fields reported so that persons with similar names are not wrongly denied credit; at credit appraisal it checks whether any director, guarantor or person in charge appears in the lists by reference to DIN or PAN, using independent sources, not the borrower's declaration, to resolve doubts about identical names. It monitors end use of funds, obtains end-use certificates from borrowers and considers legal and criminal proceedings for wrong certification. If a resolution under the IBC or the resolution framework results in a change in management and control, the name of the borrower and its promoters and directors is removed from the list after implementation and the penal measures on the new entity cease, but the one-year and five-year bars continue for erstwhile promoters and their associated entities.

When default is not wilful and the unit is viable and the promoter keen to continue, banks restructure the credit facilities on revised cash flow estimates. A restructured account is one where the bank, for economic or legal reasons relating to the borrower's financial difficulty, grants concessions that it would not otherwise consider; restructuring normally involves modification of the terms of the advances or securities such as alteration of the payment period, payable amount, amount of instalments or rate of interest, roll over of credit facilities, sanction of additional credit or release of additional funds for an account in default to cure the default, enhancement of existing credit limits, and compromise settlements where time for payment exceeds three months. The courseware lists concessions: elongation of repayment, fresh moratorium, balloon repayment, reduction in pricing and margin, sanction of fresh facilities, capitalisation of unpaid interest and instalments, conversion of outstanding in working capital into term loans, and devolved LCs and invoked guarantees converted into medium or long term loans. Restructuring is not taken up unless financial viability is established and there is a reasonable certainty of repayment; restructuring done without checking cash flows is an attempt at evergreening a weak credit facility and invites supervisory action; any action by a bank intended to conceal the actual status of accounts or evergreen stressed accounts invites supervisory and enforcement action including higher provisioning and monetary penalties.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 514-517; RBI_RSA_2025 paragraphs 6(12) and 21

facts.statement: When a default is not resolved the bank follows rectification, restructuring and recovery. Rectification covers regularisation (persuading the borrower to remit the unpaid amount and be prompt in future) and exit from the account (the bank's first effort, possible only when symptoms of stress are detected very early so the borrower can shift to another bank with a different risk appetite; in a consortium or multiple banking arrangement others may take up the exiting bank's share, while in sole banking exit is difficult; tactics include withdrawing concessions and priorities, enforcing covenants in letter and spirit, ignoring pleadings for excess drawing, reducing limits and declining all requests for excess drawings). Restructuring means rephasing or realignment, concessions and relaxations and additional finance. Recovery covers legal action, compromise and write off. In the bank's statement of options, the timely choice and an appropriate strategy play a very important role in achieving the best recovery for any stressed asset.

Recovery forums (courseware account): a suit in the Civil Court where the recoverable amount is less than Rs 20 lakh (all parties joined as defendants, interim reliefs, plaint signed by the authorised official, a preliminary decree, payment within six months and execution within a limitation period of 12 years); Debt Recovery Tribunals created for banks and financial institutions for recovery cases of Rs 20 lakh and above (NBFCs with assets above Rs 100 crore can also file there; the filing process is nearly the same as a civil suit but the procedure is summary); Lok Adalats under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987; the SARFAESI Act, 2002, which allows enforcement of security interest without the intervention of courts or tribunals (notice of demand for 60 days, possession and sale, a central registry through CERSAI, and a priority for registered secured creditors); and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 as a single law for insolvency and bankruptcy, which has proved an effective tool for banks. RBI Directions on Lok Adalats: the monetary ceiling of cases referred to Lok Adalats organised by Civil Courts is Rs 20 lakh; a bank may participate in Lok Adalats organised by DRTs or DRATs for cases of Rs 10 lakh and above; and banks are encouraged to use Lok Adalats for recovery of personal loans, credit card loans or housing loans of less than Rs 10 lakh.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 515-517 (statutory statements courseware only); RBI_RSA_2025 paragraph 102

facts.statement: Compromise settlement: the objective is to maximise the possible recovery from a distressed borrower at minimum expense in the best interest of the bank; it is not available to borrowers as a right but is a discretion exercised on commercial judgement. The courseware states the cardinal principle that the present value of the compromise offer should be higher than the present value of the realisable value of the available security. A compromise where the time for paying the settlement amount exceeds three months, a part settlement, and an arrangement under which the bank recognises claims on contingent future recoveries on its balance sheet are treated as restructuring. Board policies cover the process (minimum ageing, deterioration in collateral value), staff accountability, permissible sacrifice and valuation of security, and delegation of approval to an authority at least one level higher than the sanctioning authority (an official who took part in sanctioning the loan takes no part in approving the compromise); proposals for borrowers classified as fraud or wilful default need approval of the Management Committee of the Board (or the Board where the Management Committee originally approved the exposure). A compromise with a fraud or wilful default borrower is permitted without prejudice to criminal proceedings and the penal measures; where recovery proceedings are pending in a judicial forum, the settlement needs a consent decree. There is a cooling period before fresh exposure to a borrower who had a compromise settlement, with a floor of 12 months for exposures other than farm credit. Reporting of compromise settlements and technical write-offs goes to the next higher authority at least quarterly, and to the Board for those approved by the MD and CEO or a Board level committee.
facts.locator: RBI_RSA_2025 paragraphs 12 and 87-101; S01 printed p. 517

facts.statement: A technical write-off is where NPAs remain outstanding at the borrower's loan account level but are written off (fully or partly) by a bank only for accounting purposes, without waiver of claims against the borrower and without prejudice to recovery. It is an accounting procedure to cleanse balance sheets of bad debts that are unrecoverable or whose recovery would consume disproportionate resources; the legal obligation of the borrower and the costs of default to the borrower stay unchanged. In a partial technical write-off the prudential requirements for the residual exposure, including provisioning and asset classification, are with reference to the original exposure, and the provision including the amount of the partial write-off meets the provisioning requirement on the gross value of the asset. The courseware describes the write off as the last step when efforts to recover are exhausted: the outstanding is written off against the provision made for the account, any excess being debited to the profit and loss account; the write off does not mean the borrower's liability has ended and the bank has the right to appropriate any later recovery; it should not be the first desired course but saves time and time-value of money when done at the right time. The cooling period for exposures after technical write-offs is as per the Board approved policy.
facts.locator: RBI_RSA_2025 paragraphs 6(18) and 92-97; S01 printed p. 517

payload.title: Credit default, stressed assets and the provision coverage ratio
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Credit default** is the **inability or unwillingness** of a customer or counterparty to meet a commitment.

| Business | What a default looks like |
| --- | --- |
| **Direct lending** | **Principal or interest** not paid as per terms |
| **Guarantees and LCs** | Constituent does **not provide funds** when the liability **crystallises** |
| **Treasury** | Contract payments **not forthcoming** or **cease** |
| **Securities trading** | **Funds or securities settlement** not effected |
| **Cross-border exposure** | The **sovereign stops** availability or free transfer of **foreign currency** |

**Stressed assets:** default has **already happened** or faces a **reasonably certain prospect** of default. Example: a **term loan for an industrial project whose implementation was abandoned** is stressed **even though no instalment is due yet**.

**Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) = provisioning / gross NPAs**: how much the bank has set aside against loan losses.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Stress is recognised before NPA status: the SMA categories in the framework card capture early stages.

self_check.expected_takeaway: The ratio of provisioning to gross non-performing assets.

payload.title: Provision coverage ratio
payload.core_explanation_md: A bank has gross NPAs of Rs 150 crore and provisions held against them of Rs 60 crore. Find the provision coverage ratio, and the PCR if the provisions rise to Rs 90 crore.
payload.final_answer_with_unit: PCR is 40.00 per cent; it rises to 60.00 per cent if provisions rise to Rs 90 crore

self_check.prompt_text: Does PCR change if gross NPAs rise while provisions stay the same?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes: it falls, because the same provisions cover a larger NPA stock.

payload.title: How a wilful defaulter is identified
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Principles:** look at the **track record**, not isolated transactions; the default must be **intentional, deliberate and calculated**.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | **Identification Committee** examines the evidence |
| 2 | **Show-cause notice** with all material; submissions within **21 days** |
| 3 | Proposal to the **Review Committee** with **written reasons** |
| 4 | Person has **15 days** to give a **written representation** |
| 5 | **Personal hearing** by the Review Committee |
| 6 | **Reasoned order** communicated. No right to a **lawyer** (in-house process) |

**Committees:** **Identification:** a **whole-time director (not the MD and CEO)** plus **two senior officials**. **Review:** the **MD and CEO** plus **two independent or non-executive directors**; **different people** from the Identification Committee.

**Non-executive, independent or nominee directors** are **not** wilful defaulters unless it is **conclusively shown** that the default had their **consent or connivance**, or they **knew from board minutes** and **did not record objection**.

**When:** examine wilful default in all **NPAs of Rs 25 lakh and above**; complete classification **within six months** of NPA classification.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The 2025 text fixes the six-month limit from the NPA date.

self_check.prompt_text: Within how many days of the show-cause notice must the person respond?

payload.title: Penal measures and reporting on wilful defaulters
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Penal measures**

- **No additional credit** to the wilful defaulter or **associated entities**; the bar **lasts one year after removal** from the list.
- **No credit for new ventures for five years after removal**.
- **Restructuring** only as the Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions allow.
- **Covenant:** the borrower will **not induct a person from the list** on its board or management; **no renewal, enhancement, fresh credit or restructuring** while such a person remains.
- **Associated entities:** a **subsidiary, joint venture or associate**; for a **natural person**, entities where he is **promoter, director or in charge of management**.
- **Guarantors** who refuse to pay on demand may be classified too; **group companies** whose guarantees are not honoured are considered.

**Reporting (to all Credit Information Companies, monthly)**

- **Large defaulters** (Rs 1 crore and above; suit-filed, or doubtful or loss).
- **Wilful defaulters** (suit-filed and non-suit-filed).
- **Removal** within **30 days** after the outstanding falls below **Rs 25 lakh**, **except** in a **compromise**: the name stays until the **compromise amount is fully paid**.
- Include the **Director Identification Number (DIN)** so similar names are not wrongly denied credit; at appraisal check directors, guarantors and persons in charge in the lists by **DIN or PAN**, confirming identity from **independent sources**.

**After a resolution that changes management and control** (IBC or the resolution framework): the borrower and its promoters and directors are **removed from the list** and penal measures on the **new entity** cease; the **one- and five-year bars continue for erstwhile promoters**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Before a bank transfers a defaulted loan of Rs 25 lakh and above, it must test for wilful default first.

self_check.prompt_text: For how long after removal from the list is a new venture barred from bank credit?

payload.title: Restructuring: what it is and when it is allowed
payload.core_explanation_md:
If the default is **not wilful**, the unit is **viable** and the promoter is **keen to continue**, banks **restructure** on revised cash flow estimates.

**Restructuring:** the bank, **for economic or legal reasons relating to the borrower's financial difficulty**, grants **concessions it would not otherwise consider**: change in **payment period, amount or instalment, rate of interest**; **roll over**; **additional credit** for an account in default to cure it; **enhanced limits**; **compromise** where payment takes **more than three months**.

**Concessions the courseware lists:** **elongation**, **fresh moratorium**, **balloon repayment**, **cut in pricing and margin**, **fresh facilities**, **capitalisation** of unpaid interest and instalments, **conversion of working capital outstanding into term loans**, and **devolved LCs and invoked guarantees converted to medium or long term loans**.

**Conditions:** **no restructuring unless financial viability is established** and repayment is **reasonably certain**. Restructuring **without checking cash flows** is **evergreening** and invites supervisory action.

**Supervisory action:** any step meant to **conceal the true status** of accounts or **evergreen** stressed accounts brings **higher provisioning** and **monetary penalties**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Restructuring normally needs the borrower's consent and a changed loan agreement.

self_check.prompt_text: Is a compromise paid over six months a restructuring?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes: a compromise where the time for payment exceeds three months is treated as restructuring.

payload.title: Rectification, restructuring and recovery
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Route | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Rectification** | **Regularisation** (persuade the borrower to pay the overdue and stay prompt) and **exit** |
| **Restructuring** | **Rephasing or realignment**, **concessions and relaxations**, **additional finance** |
| **Recovery** | **Legal action**, **compromise**, **write off** |

**Exit:** the bank's **first effort**, but possible only if stress is **detected very early**, so the borrower can **move to a bank with a different risk appetite**. In **consortium or multiple banking**, others may take the exiting bank's share; in **sole banking** it is **hard**.

**Tactics for exit:** **withdraw concessions and priorities**, **enforce covenants in letter and spirit**, **ignore pleas for excess drawing**, **reduce limits**, **decline excess drawings**.

The **timing and choice** of strategy are decisive for recovery.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Early detection keeps all three routes open.

self_check.prompt_text: Which route is the bank's first effort in a stressed account?

payload.title: Recovery forums
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Forum | Courseware account | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Civil Court** | Recoverable amount **below Rs 20 lakh**; plaint signed by the authorised official; preliminary decree, payment within **six months**, execution within **12 years** | statutory limits as the courseware states (needs_review) |
| **Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT)** | **Rs 20 lakh and above**; NBFCs with assets above **Rs 100 crore** can file; **summary** procedure | statutory (needs_review) |
| **Lok Adalat** | Settlement forum under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987** | RBI limits below |
| **SARFAESI Act, 2002** | Enforce **security interest without courts or tribunals**: **demand notice of 60 days**, **possession and sale**; **CERSAI** records; registered secured creditors have **priority** | statutory (needs_review) |
| **IBC, 2016** | **Single law** on insolvency and bankruptcy; an effective tool for banks | taught in the next unit |

**RBI limits for Lok Adalats**

- Civil Court Lok Adalats: cases up to **Rs 20 lakh**.
- **DRT or DRAT Lok Adalats:** a bank may take part for cases of **Rs 10 lakh and above**.
- Banks are **encouraged** to use Lok Adalats for **personal loans, credit card loans and housing loans of less than Rs 10 lakh**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware says banks may refer DRT Lok Adalat cases irrespective of amount; the 2025 Directions say Rs 10 lakh and above.

self_check.prompt_text: Up to what amount may a bank refer cases to a Lok Adalat organised by a civil court?

payload.title: Compromise settlements
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Objective:** **maximise recovery at minimum expense**, in the bank's best interest. **Not a right**: a **discretion** exercised on **commercial judgement**.

**Courseware principle:** the **present value of the compromise offer** must be **higher than** the **present value of the realisable value of the security**.

**Treated as restructuring:**

- payment of the settlement amount takes **more than three months**;
- a **part settlement**;
- an arrangement where the bank puts **claims on contingent future recoveries** on its balance sheet.

**Governance**

- Board policy: **process** (minimum ageing, fall in collateral value), **staff accountability**, **permissible sacrifice**, **valuation** of security.
- **Approval** one **level above** the sanctioning authority; **anyone who sanctioned the loan** takes **no part** in approving the compromise.
- **Fraud or wilful default** borrowers: **Management Committee of the Board** (or the Board where the Management Committee made the original approval).
- **Pending suit:** a **consent decree** is needed.
- **Cooling period** before fresh exposure: floor of **12 months** (other than farm credit).
- **Reporting** at least **quarterly** to the next higher authority; to the **Board** for approvals by the **MD and CEO** or a Board committee.

A compromise with a fraud or wilful default borrower is allowed **without prejudice to criminal proceedings and penal measures**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: A compromise ends the bank's relationship with the borrower; a restructuring continues it.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the floor for the cooling period before fresh exposure to a borrower after a compromise (other than farm credit)?

payload.title: Technical write-off and write off
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Technical write-off:** NPAs stay **outstanding in the borrower's account** but are **written off for accounting only**, **fully or partly**, with **no waiver of claims** and no harm to **recovery**.

- It **cleanses the balance sheet** of debts that are **unrecoverable** or whose recovery would **cost too much**.
- The **borrower's legal obligation** and the **costs of default** to the borrower are **unchanged**.
- **Partial technical write-off:** prudential rules (**provisioning, asset classification**) apply with reference to the **original exposure**; the **provision plus the amount written off** must meet the **requirement on the gross value**.
- **Cooling period** after a technical write-off: as per **Board policy**.

**Write off (courseware):** when **recovery efforts are exhausted**, the outstanding is written off **against the provision**, with any **excess charged to profit and loss**. It **does not end the borrower's liability**; the bank may **appropriate any later recovery**. It is **not the first choice** but saves **time and time-value** when done at the right time.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Technical write-offs are reported quarterly to a higher authority along with compromise settlements.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a technical write-off waive the borrower's liability?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: claims against the borrower continue and recovery is not prejudiced.

payload.title: Is the compromise offer acceptable?

The bank's discount rate is 10 per cent a year. Apply the courseware principle, and say how the Directions would treat a settlement paid in two equal instalments six months and nine months from now.

unresolved: The meaning of credit default and stressed assets, the options (rectification, restructuring, recovery), the description of recovery forums and the principle for compromise are the courseware's account (S01 printed pp. 512 to 517, PDF pp. 527 to 532). Wilful default (Directions of 28 November 2025), compromise settlements, technical write-offs, Lok Adalats and the provision coverage ratio are taught from RBI_WD_2025, RBI_RSA_2025 paragraphs 84-102 and RBI_IRACP_2025 paragraph 5(9); the courseware cites the 30 July 2024 master direction on wilful defaulters and the 2016 circular on publishing photographs, which the 2025 Directions replace.

A 27 April 2026 amendment to the wilful defaulter Directions (RBI/2026-27/28, effective 1 April 2027) was reported in a search summary but not retrieved; it is not taught (after the cut-off). The 2025 text (paragraph 6(2)) requires classification within six months of the account becoming an NPA.

The courseware's statements on the Civil Court (Rs 20 lakh), Debt Recovery Tribunals (Rs 20 lakh and above, NBFCs with assets above Rs 100 crore), the SARFAESI Act (60 days notice, 2004 amendment, tribunal appeal with 50 per cent deposit, 28 asset reconstruction companies as of November 2021) and the Limitation period (12 years for execution) are statutory statements not checked against the Acts or later changes (needs_review). The courseware says banks may refer DRT Lok Adalat cases irrespective of the amount; RBI_RSA_2025 paragraph 102 says banks may participate in DRT or DRAT Lok Adalats for cases of Rs 10 lakh and above, which is taught.

The courseware's account of the publication of photographs of wilful defaulters (items i to iv, NHRC remark, education loan defaulters) is not taught beyond the requirement that the Board policy has non-discriminatory criteria (RBI_WD_2025 paragraph 4).

Amendments marked after 30 June 2026 in RBI_RSA_2025 (Chapter VI-A calamities, SNFA paragraphs) are not taught. The amendment dated 27 April 2026 on the timeline for declaring wilful defaulters took effect from 1 April 2027 and is not taught.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
